note: Techniques of MOOC part 12: generic classes with one and two type parameters (also nested, as in Box<List<Double>>), a generic interface with a generic and a non-generic class that implement it, generic methods, a list of its own (an array that grows, add, contains, indexOf, remove with shifting, and its own index error) that compiles with javac's note about unchecked operations, a hash map of its own with buckets of key-value pairs (put, get, remove, growing, and String keys with negative hash codes), Random with seeds (nextInt with and without a bound and with an origin, nextDouble, nextBoolean, nextGaussian, ints, Collections.shuffle), two-dimensional arrays (filled, row and column sums, jagged rows, Arrays.deepToString, String[][], copies of rows, the rows of a boolean grid created in one new (cloned, copied, swapped, kept in a list, instanceof, deepEquals), three dimensions), and the messages of the part's mistakes caught: a negative array size, a grid index, a bound of 0, a negative list capacity and an Object[] used as a String[]
